You’ll be supported with digital tools, industry leading training, ongoing coaching, and backed by one of the most recognized brands in banking. This role offers a clear platform for career growth for experienced professionals who excel at building trust, managing a portfolio, and delivering holistic, multi product solutions. jobs.description: Job Description Summary The Assistant Operational Controller Europe is responsible for supporting the Europe Operational Controller in controllership activities relating to GE HealthCare's (GEHC) operations, non-commercial processes and legal entities in the Europe Zone. The role supports financial reporting and monitoring, technical controllership guidance, US GAAP balance sheet integrity and operating mechanisms to identify, understand and manage non-commercial business risks. The Assistant Operational Controller will partner with Zone Finance, Operational teams, Local Country Teams (LCTs), Non-Commercial COE/BPO teams, Statutory and Tax teams, Treasury, HR Operations and Global Controllership to ensure timely and accurate monthly and quarterly US GAAP closing and reporting, compliance with GEHC policies, Sarbanes-Oxley requirements and effective execution of operational controllership processes. The role reports to the Europe Operational Controller. THIS ROLE IS OPEN IN ALL LOCATIONS IN EUROPE ZONE EVEN IF NOT INCLUDED IN THE ROLE POSTING LOCATION. NO RELOCATION REQUIRED. Job Description Essential Responsibilities Duties include (but are not limited to): Support the Europe Operational Controller on non-commercial, operational and technical controllership aspects of the business across the Europe Zone. Support legal entity management activities, including legal entity rationalization, ERP reduction initiatives, capital structure remediation and coordination of legal entity cash flow management with Treasury, Tax, Controllership and local finance teams. Support establishment, documentation and continuous improvement of Standard Work for operational and transactional processes impacting the financial statements, including closing, reporting and analysis. Support key non-commercial processes such as Logistics, Restructuring, Grants, Sales Incentive Compensation, Fleet, Dilapidation and other operational balance sheet areas. Assist in quarterly risk reviews with Global Markets Region Controller and Global Markets Region CFO, quarterly LCT balance sheet reviews and Financial Review Process (FRP) submissions with Global Controllership. Drive consistent execution of monthly and quarterly close procedures, including account reconciliations, reconciliation quality reviews, GEHC Data Request submissions, representation letters and adjusting entries. Perform financial analysis of non-commercial balance sheet accounts to ensure compliance, integrity of balances, accurate financial reporting and effectiveness of business processes. Ensure non-commercial account reconciliations are completed accurately, supported by appropriate documentation and within GEHC corporate guidelines. Monitor internal controls in line with local statutory requirements, GEHC GAP, US GAAP and corporate policies; identify financial risks and opportunities and support timely remediation actions. Support compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley 404 requirements for non-commercial and operational controls, excluding commercial controls. Coordinate with GEHC Internal Audit and external auditors to support audit requests, issue remediation, corrective action plans and prevention of recurring control issues. Support simplification initiatives across the Europe Zone to reduce process complexity and enable local teams to focus on value-added analytical and strategic activities. Support GEHC initiatives, integration projects, IT finance projects, Digital Core Transformation and Global Markets region transformation projects related to non-commercial processes and systems. Partner with LCT Statutory and Tax Leaders to support efficient statutory and tax processes, audit planning, audit debriefs, audit fee management and process performance metrics. Partner with Payroll Tax Leaders and HR Operations to support efficient payroll tax audit processes and improvements to payroll tax operations. Prepare analyses, reports and presentations for Europe Operational Controller, Europe Zone Controller, Global Markets Controllership and other finance leadership stakeholders as required. Qualifications Qualified ACA, ACCA, CPA, CA, CIMA or Master’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or other business-related field, with proven experience in accounting, controllership, audit or finance. Experience in multinational organizations with exposure to operational accounting, legal entity controllership, financial reporting, internal controls, statutory processes and US GAAP is preferred. Desired Characteristics External Auditing Firm graduate, Big Four experience preferred Demonstrates strong understanding of U.S. GAAP, revenue recognition principles, local GAAP considerations and authoritative accounting literature. Experience supporting cross-functional projects, process improvements or standardization initiatives within operations or finance functions. Multi-country accounting, controllership or commercial finance experience preferred. Capable of building strong relationships with finance and non-finance colleagues across a matrix organization. Strong interpersonal skills and excellent verbal/written communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex accounting and business issues in a clear and concise manner. Integrity: accepting and adhering to high moral, ethical and personal values in decisions, communications, actions and when dealing with others. Clear thinking, problem-solving mindset and ability to quickly grasp new ideas, assess risks and propose workable solutions. Adaptable/Flexible: open to change in response to new information and in different or unexpected circumstances. Confidence and influencing skills across business functions, with ability to challenge constructively and escalate appropriately. Self-starter and quick learner with strong ownership mindset and commitment to meet deadlines. Strong experience in internal controls, including Sarbanes-Oxley 404 requirements. Strong attention to detail, analytical capability and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Experience with SAP, Oracle or other large ERP systems preferred; advanced Excel and financial analytics skills desirable. Inclusion and Diversity GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law. Our total rewards are designed to fuel your ambition by providing the flexibility and support you need to turn your ideas into impactful realities. Our compensation and benefits align with what you'd expect from an organization of global reach and scale. You'll find yourself surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration, and support. IN FRENCH: Résumé du poste L'Assistant(e) Contrôleur(se) Opérationnel(le) Europe est chargé(e) de soutenir le Contrôleur Opérationnel Europe dans les activités de contrôle financier liées aux opérations de GE HealthCare (GEHC), aux processus non commerciaux et aux entités juridiques de la zone Europe. Le poste contribue au reporting financier et à son suivi, fournit des conseils techniques en matière de contrôle financier, veille à l'intégrité du bilan selon les normes US GAAP et met en œuvre des mécanismes opérationnels permettant d'identifier, de comprendre et de gérer les risques liés aux activités non commerciales. L'Assistant(e) Contrôleur(se) Opérationnel(le) travaillera en partenariat avec les équipes Finance de la zone, les équipes opérationnelles, les équipes locales pays (LCT), les équipes COE/BPO des activités non commerciales, les équipes Statutaire et Fiscalité, la Trésorerie, les Opérations RH et l'organisation Global Controllership afin de garantir la clôture et le reporting mensuels et trimestriels US GAAP dans les délais, le respect des politiques GEHC, des exigences Sarbanes-Oxley ainsi qu'une exécution efficace des processus de contrôle opérationnel. Le poste est rattaché au Contrôleur Opérationnel Europe. Ce poste est ouvert dans tous les pays de la zone Europe, même si certains sites ne sont pas mentionnés dans l’offre d’emploi. Aucune mobilité géographique ni relocalisation n’est requise. Responsabilités principales Les responsabilités comprennent notamment : Soutenir le Contrôleur Opérationnel Europe sur les aspects de contrôle financier non commerciaux, opérationnels et techniques au sein de la zone Europe. Participer à la gestion des entités juridiques, notamment les projets de rationalisation des entités, de réduction du nombre d'ERP, d'optimisation des structures de capital et la coordination de la gestion des flux de trésorerie avec les équipes Trésorerie, Fiscalité, Contrôle Financier et Finances locales. Contribuer à la mise en place, à la documentation et à l'amélioration continue des procédures standardisées (Standard Work) pour les processus opérationnels et transactionnels impactant les états financiers. Soutenir les principaux processus non commerciaux tels que la Logistique, la Restructuration, les Subventions, la Rémunération Variable des Ventes, la Gestion de Flotte, les obligations locatives et autres postes opérationnels du bilan. Participer aux revues trimestrielles des risques avec le Regional Controller et le CFO de Global Markets, aux revues trimestrielles des bilans des équipes locales ainsi qu'aux soumissions du Financial Review Process (FRP) auprès du Global Controllership. Contribuer à l'exécution cohérente des procédures de clôture mensuelles et trimestrielles, y compris les rapprochements de comptes, les revues qualité des rapprochements, les soumissions des Data Requests GEHC, les lettres de représentation et les écritures d'ajustement. Réaliser des analyses financières des comptes de bilan non commerciaux afin de garantir leur conformité, leur intégrité, l'exactitude du reporting financier et l'efficacité des processus opérationnels. Veiller à ce que les rapprochements de comptes non commerciaux soient réalisés avec exactitude, correctement documentés et conformes aux directives de GEHC. Surveiller les contrôles internes conformément aux obligations légales locales, aux principes GEHC GAP, aux normes US GAAP et aux politiques de l'entreprise ; identifier les risques et opportunités financiers et soutenir les actions correctives nécessaires. Soutenir la conformité aux exigences Sarbanes-Oxley 404 relatives aux contrôles non commerciaux et opérationnels. Coordonner les interactions avec l'Audit Interne GEHC et les auditeurs externes afin de répondre aux demandes d'audit, soutenir les plans de remédiation et prévenir la récurrence des problèmes de contrôle. Participer aux initiatives de simplification à travers la zone Europe afin de réduire la complexité des processus et permettre aux équipes locales de se concentrer sur des activités à forte valeur ajoutée. Soutenir les initiatives GEHC, les projets d'intégration, les projets Finance-IT, la transformation Digital Core ainsi que les programmes de transformation Global Markets liés aux processus et systèmes non commerciaux. Collaborer avec les responsables Statutaire et Fiscalité afin d'améliorer l'efficacité des processus réglementaires et fiscaux, la planification des audits, les débriefings, la gestion des honoraires d'audit et les indicateurs de performance. Collaborer avec les responsables Fiscalité Paie et les équipes RH afin d'améliorer les audits liés à la paie et les opérations fiscales associées. Préparer des analyses, rapports et présentations pour le Contrôleur Opérationnel Europe, le Contrôleur de Zone Europe, le Global Markets Controllership et d'autres parties prenantes de la direction financière. ​ Qualifications requises Diplôme professionnel de type ACA, ACCA, CPA, CA ou CIMA, ou Master en Comptabilité, Finance ou domaine équivalent. Expérience confirmée et évolutive en comptabilité, contrôle financier, audit ou finance. Expérience dans des organisations multinationales avec une exposition à la comptabilité opérationnelle, au contrôle des entités juridiques, au reporting financier, aux contrôles internes, aux processus statutaires et aux normes US GAAP est fortement souhaitée. ​ Profil recherché Expérience dans un cabinet d'audit externe, idéalement Big Four. Solide maîtrise des normes US GAAP, des principes de reconnaissance du chiffre d'affaires, des normes comptables locales et de la littérature comptable de référence. Expérience dans la gestion de projets transverses, d'amélioration de processus ou de standardisation au sein des fonctions Finance ou Opérations. Une expérience internationale, multi-pays, en comptabilité, contrôle financier ou finance commerciale est un atout. Capacité à développer des relations solides avec des interlocuteurs financiers et non financiers dans une organisation matricielle. Excellentes compétences relationnelles et de communication écrite et orale, avec la capacité d'expliquer clairement des problématiques comptables complexes. Intégrité et respect de normes éthiques élevées. Esprit analytique, capacité de résolution de problèmes et aptitude à évaluer rapidement les risques tout en proposant des solutions pragmatiques. Flexibilité et capacité d'adaptation dans un environnement en évolution. Capacité d'influence et d'assertivité constructive auprès des différentes fonctions de l'entreprise. Autonomie, sens des responsabilités et capacité à respecter des délais exigeants. Solide expérience des contrôles internes, y compris des exigences Sarbanes-Oxley 404. Grande rigueur, souci du détail et aptitude à gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément. Expérience des systèmes ERP tels que SAP ou Oracle est appréciée ; une maîtrise avancée d'Excel et des outils d'analyse financière constitue un avantage. Inclusion et diversité GE HealthCare est un employeur offrant l'égalité des chances où l'inclusion compte. Les décisions relatives à l'emploi sont prises sans tenir compte de l’origine nationale ou ethnique, de la religion, du sexe, de l'orientation sexuelle, de l'identité ou de l'expression de genre, de l'âge, du handicap, du statut d'ancien combattant protégé ou d'autres caractéristiques protégées par la loi. Nos rémunérations totales sont conçues pour libérer votre ambition en vous donnant la motivation et la flexibilité dont vous avez besoin pour transformer vos idées en réalités qui changent le monde. Nos salaires et nos avantages sociaux correspondent à tout ce que vous attendez d’une organisation ayant une dimension internationale, avec des possibilités de développement de carrière, dans une culture qui favorise la collaboration et le soutien. Additional Information Relocation Assistance Provided: No

jobs.description: Job Description Summary The Site Manager at Clinch River is responsible for the oversight and execution of construction, installation, and commissioning on the customer site. This role encompasses the entire project lifecycle from site mobilization through civil works, erection, and commissioning, alongside associated management activities. The Site Manager owns and influences site budgets and operating plans, operating under established company policy. Working closely with cross-functional teams, this role demands high levels of evaluative judgment and operational acumen to ensure all site operations align with company objectives, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements, quality, and efficiency while fostering a productive work environment. Job Description Roles and Responsibilities Site Operations & Project Leadership: Lead and oversee the full scope of site activities during the Inquiry to Order (ITO) and/or Order to Remittance (OTR) phases for construction, installation, and commissioning. Act as the primary on-site leader, directly reporting to the Project Director.. Team & Resource Management: Manage, lead, and develop the site team, including contractors and sub-contractors, fostering a collaborative and high-performance environment. Efficiently manage all site resources and logistics, including equipment, materials, and facility maintenance. Compliance & Standards: Ensure strict adherence to project schedules, quality standards, and cost parameters in compliance with contractual obligations, company policies, and all local, state, and federal regulations. Risk Management & Problem Solving: Proactively monitor project progress, identify potential risks, and develop effective mitigation strategies. Leverage expertise to find creative solutions for business challenges and recommend best practices to improve products, processes or services. Performance & Continuous Improvement: Drive operational excellence through regular site inspections and audits. Interpret internal and external business challenges and recommend best practices to improve products, processes, or services, utilizing an understanding of industry trends to inform decision-making. Stakeholder Engagement & Communication: Maintain accurate site records, including comprehensive progress reports, daily logs, safety documentation, and quality control checks. Effectively communicate complex messages and negotiate internally to gain alignment, influencing peers and presenting business or technical solutions to leaders. Also, engage and potentially negotiate with external partners, vendors, customers, and regulatory bodies. Safety & Quality Assurance: Implement and rigorously enforce comprehensive safety programs and protocols to ensure a zero-incident culture and uphold the highest quality standards on site. Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field. Minimum of 8-10 years of experience in site management or a similar leadership role, preferably in a relevant industry. Proven track record of successfully managing complex projects on time and within budget. Strong understanding of project management principles, construction methods, and safety regulations. Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple priorities. Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree or professional certifications (e.g., PMP, OSHA 30). Experience specifically within the Clinch River area or similar operational environments. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder management Extensive understanding of power generation and the nuclear industry Note: To comply with US immigration and other legal requirements, it is necessary to specify the minimum number of years' experience required for any role based within the USA. Operational Excellence

Team Leadership

Company Introduction:

Coupang is reimagining the shopping experience with the goal of wowing each customer from the instant they open the Coupang app to the moment an order is delivered to their door.

Our services in Taiwan include “Rocket Delivery” which offers next-day delivery for a wide selection of items at affordable prices, “Rocket Oversea” which offers free international delivery on millions of best-selling products from Korea, the U.S., and beyond.

Role Overview:

We're in search of a Staff Data Scientist to join our supply chain management technology team. This role is ideal for someone deeply passionate about applied research, AI/ML, and Operations Research, eager to collaborate across product, engineering, business, and operations to tackle the most complex challenges in supply chain management. The successful candidate will thrive in an interdisciplinary environment, adept at developing production solutions from scratch or enhancing existing ones, and will play a pivotal role in shaping and executing the vision for automating supply chain management.

What You Will Do:

• Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including product, engineering, and business, to identify opportunities for enhancing our technology products, translating ambiguous business requirements into practical solutions.
• Conduct comprehensive research and analysis to inform model development, establishing metrics and success criteria for evaluating solution effectiveness
• Deliver data-driven solutions to support automated decision-making at scale, leveraging advanced Statistics, Machine Learning, and Operations Research techniques to optimize business processes and make data-driven decisions/predictions
• Analyze/solve complex data problems using innovative methods, such as deep learning, and communicate findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders through clear and concise reports and presentations
• Provide analysis for launched solutions to quantify outcomes based on real-world results, identifying areas for improvement and opportunities for future development

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's/Master's degree in mathematics/statistics, computer science/engineering, industrial engineering, operations research, or any other quantitative disciplines, with 5+ years of relevant experience working in industry or academia
• Hands-on experience in statistics/ML fundamentals and demonstrated experience in Python, SQL, and basic visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI)
• Strong critical thinking skills and ability to solve ambiguous problems supported by solid knowledge of data science and machine learning fundamentals, with proven experience to formulate business problems to data science solutions
• Ability to conduct analysis independently for a business problem through data manipulation, hypothesis formulation, experiment design, and statistical analysis
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills to effectively engage with technical and business stakeholders at all levels, including presentation development and delivery

Preferred Qualifications:

• Strong ability to model ambiguous business and operational problems at the appropriate level of abstraction, with a focus on delivering practical solutions
• Advanced proficiency with machine learning frameworks, tools, and languages such as Python, R, Java, TensorFlow, and PyTorch, with experience building ML/DL models to handle large-scale datasets
• Proven experience in AI/ML-driven demand forecasting, lead time prediction, causal models, fulfillment rate prediction, with the ability to collaborate with ML Engineers and Data Analysts to optimize model development and deployment
• Experience designing and implementing large-scale optimization solutions for complex business problems
• Expertise in developing and deploying advanced algorithms, including decomposition methods, heuristics/metaheuristics, and hybrid methods
• Familiarity with Big Data ecosystem (Spark, Hive, HBase) and SQL/NoSQL (Redis/MongoDB) for handling complex data transformations and analysis
• A deep understanding of the e-commerce business domain and the ability to apply cutting-edge models into production environments, driving measurable results

This role is part of a highly technical silicon validation team responsible for Memory/SSD sub‑system. • Enable new memory products and configurations

• Requires good written and oral communication skills.

• Working knowledge of lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic and protocol analyzers

jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) brings new services and features to customers at an unprecedented cadence — more than 3,000 launches a year, and accelerating as the AI landscape evolves. Behind that velocity is the Launch Operations team, which owns the process that governs the lifecycle of bringing every AWS capability to customers, from intake through customer availability. We turn AWS’s innovation velocity into a durable Marketing advantage: driving operational scale so service teams and stakeholders can focus on innovation, and improving signal-to-noise so the most important news reaches customers and enables field sales and partner teams to engage around the launches that matter most.

We are looking for a Program Manager to help run the programs that make this possible. Working closely with senior program managers and stakeholders, you will help keep launches moving on time and at a high quality bar — coordinating across product managers, marketing, engineering, security, legal, and field teams, tracking deliverables, and surfacing risks early. This is a role for someone who is organized, resourceful, and eager to grow in a high-visibility, cross-functional environment where the details matter and the scale is significant. You will learn the launch process end to end, and as you do, you will spot where manual coordination slows launches down and help implement the improvements that make the next cycle smoother.

Key job responsibilities
1. Support the end-to-end launch operations program including tracking milestones and deliverables, maintaining schedules, and surfacing risks across multiple concurrent launches.

2. Coordinate with product managers, marketing, engineering, security, legal, and field teams to keep launches moving from intake to customer availability and help remove blockers.

3. Help identify process gaps in how launches move through the pipeline and contribute to improvements that raise quality and reduce cycle time.

4. Maintain program dashboards and status reporting, ensuring stakeholders have accurate, timely visibility into launch progress.

5. Track program metrics and help improve signal-to-noise so the most important launches are elevated to customers.

6. Apply generative AI tools including Amazon Quick to streamline documentation, status reporting, and program analysis.

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing the launch pipeline and flagging any launches at risk of slipping, then follow up with the relevant task owners to keep them on track. Mid-morning, you join a working session with product and marketing partners to walk through upcoming launches and capture next steps. After lunch, you update the program dashboard and pull together a status summary for the team, highlighting progress and any open items that need attention. Between meetings, you look for small ways to remove friction in the intake process often using generative AI tooling to speed up the documentation and reporting that used to take up much of your day.

About the team
The AWS Lifecycle Marketing team shapes how the world’s leading cloud and AI portfolio reaches customers. We orchestrate how AWS launches are integrated with Marketing planning, how lifecycle changes are managed responsibly, and how the portfolio is represented across shared surfaces and priority moments — removing complexity, increasing visibility, and ensuring Marketing can act with the coordination, speed, and strategic focus the portfolio requires. Launch Operations is the connective tissue between AWS Service Engineering and AWS Marketing, and this role is a great entry point into a multi-year transformation from manual, relationship-driven coordination to scalable, data-driven platforms. If you want to work on programs that shape how millions of customers experience AWS innovation, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.description: You will own the operational enablement functions that allow ISOC (Intervention Security Operations Center) international monitoring operations to run at scale across regulated jurisdictions. This role is responsible for regulatory compliance management, technology integration coordination, vendor contract management, training and certification programs, and the standard operating procedures that ensure consistent execution regardless of location or operator. You are the person who builds the systems and frameworks that the rest of the team operates within. This is not an operations execution role. You will not manage shifts or handle alerts. You will build the compliance backbone, negotiate vendor agreements, coordinate platform deployments, develop training curricula, and maintain the audit and governance frameworks that keep operations legally sound and operationally excellent. You enable the people who execute by giving them the tools, training, standards, and contracts they need to perform. Key job responsibilities ● Own regulatory and compliance management for ISOC monitoring operations across all international jurisdictions, ensuring operations meet data protection, surveillance, and privacy requirements ● Navigate legal frameworks for remote monitoring, cross-border data transfer, and alert handling, partnering with legal counsel to translate regulatory requirements into operational procedures ● Manage vendor contracts for third party monitoring operators, including agreement negotiation, SLA definition, performance measurement, cost optimization, and renewal planning ● Coordinate technology integration across the monitoring platform, including new system deployments, platform standardization, configuration management, and tool selection ● Develop and maintain the training and certification program for ISOC analysts, including onboarding curricula, recurring proficiency assessments, and specialized skill development for new use cases ● Own the standard operating procedure (SOP) library, ensuring procedures remain current with regulatory changes, technology updates, and lessons learned from operational incidents ● Build and maintain the audit and compliance framework, including internal assessment schedules, evidence collection, regulatory reporting, and remediation tracking ● Drive operational excellence initiatives: process improvement, efficiency analysis, quality management, and standardization across international control room operations ● Support the EU Country Lead and broader ISOC leadership with operational enablement, removing barriers and providing the compliance, technology, and vendor infrastructure needed for growth A day in the life Your morning starts with reviewing a regulatory update from counsel on a pending change to monitoring consent requirements in one of your operating jurisdictions. You assess the operational impact, draft the Standard Operating Procedure revision needed, and flag the training update required for affected analysts. Mid-morning, you join a vendor performance review call to discuss compliance, staffing shortfalls, and contract renewal terms for one of your third party operator agreements. You spend part of your day working on the technology integration roadmap: coordinating with the platform team on a new system deployment timeline, validating that data handling configurations meet jurisdictional requirements, and updating the integration checklist for the operations team. After lunch, you review the latest analyst certification results from the quarterly assessment cycle, identify skill gaps, and adjust the training program accordingly. You close the day updating the compliance tracker for an upcoming audit and preparing a cost optimization proposal for the next vendor negotiation cycle. About the team ISOC (Intervention Security Operations Center) is Amazon's centralized, alert-driven security intervention capability within the Security Operations Group. Operating 24/7 control rooms across multiple global locations, ISOC receives technology-generated signals, validates threats in real time, and coordinates the appropriate response function. ISOC sits within SOG under Worldwide Operations Security (WWOS) and is positioned within the security lifecycle model as the team that owns the Intervention function. The international operations span multiple countries and regulatory environments, requiring robust compliance frameworks, standardized procedures, and coordinated enablement functions to maintain operational consistency at scale. This role provides that enablement layer, ensuring that operations teams have the regulatory clearance, technology platforms, trained workforce, and vendor support they need to deliver.
